data.name: ZOMBI
data.detailed_description:
You’re still breathing, for now, but how long will you survive the labyrinth of London’s streets and underground canals, abandoned by the outside world and surrounded by infected? The horrifying remains of humanity, ravaged by the terrifying disease, are shuffling through the streets, waiting at every turn to prey on your living flesh.

The nail-biting survival experience of ZombiU™ has been upgraded for download on next-gen consoles and PC. ZOMBI takes the power of the latest generation of hardware to bring you a new level of horror. Test your will to survive, but beware: death is permanent, and one wrong move can cause you to lose everything.

Features


PURE SURVIVAL HORROR
Resources are scarce, your enemies are numerous, and you never know when you’ll find more weapons, ammunition, first aid, or food. How you allocate your resources determines if you live or die.

WITH PERMADEATH, EVERYTHING IS AT STAKE
Survival is not guaranteed. Once you die, your character becomes infected and joins the horde of undead shambling through London. You’ll come back as an entirely new character and try to survive, again, with your first mission being to retrieve your previous character’s supplies.

BUG-OUT BAG
Your bug-out bag holds all your possessions, tools, inventory, first aid kits, maps, and more. Don’t get distracted, as zombies can attack you at any moment. If you die, your bag stays with your old character, who is now a zombie. Will you risk it all to get your bag back, or start scavenging anew?

LONDON CALLING
Survive in a city steeped in grisly history, royal secrets, and bloody tales. Navigate through the medieval Tower of London, stately Buckingham Palace, and modern streets swarming with mobs of the undead.

THE UNDEAD RETURN
Combining the horror of ZombiU with refined gameplay and upgraded graphics, ZOMBI brings the survivalist first-person shooter to next-gen consoles and PC. Adapted to a single screen experience, the active pause system still makes you vulnerable while scanning your environment, completing mini-games or searching your inventory & equipment.

data.short_description: London is falling. Are you prepared? The Last Blight is upon us. It was foretold. For the second time in history, a great plague has shrouded London in a fog of death. Big Ben tolls as thousands of unprepared die, or worse, are infected by a sickness more gruesome than death.

reviews.review:
I really try to like this game but there are actual downsides to this product, non of them as bad others try to claim but those things just should not be ignored.

This is Ubisofts attempt at Survival Horror with Zombies. It was originally released for the Wii U, i remember "Zombi U" being advertised heavily as the console itself flopped hard for Nintendo. Back then, the pad that came with the Wii U served as the mini map, scanner, radar and inventory management, quite innovative i must say. The fact that the PC port has no third party pad-thing is no surprise, hense it is integrated into the game and it functions good enough.

I did want to finish the game and its achievements since i genuinely think it is amazing for what it is, maybe it will happen someday but for now the experience has been quite frustrating.

From what i have seen in the first couple hours, the premise is based on religious world ending prophecies in which the black angels (undead, zombies etc) destroy modern society and make room for Gods "new, reorganized world". It takes place in London and, by the achievements, one will visit major locations and buildings that you'd go to as a tourist for sight seeing reasons.

In all honesty: The atmosphere and immersion in this game is absolutely incredible. Ubisoft did not hold back when designing this zombie game. Zombi takes itself very seriously and the feeling of distress, "not being safe at any point"; they nailed it. Of course the visiuals aged quite a bit but thats really a non issue since the games age obviously speaks for itself, although the stylized art direction makes up for it by carefully placed light sources and claustrophobic level design.

The story is guided by the one dude who "always knew that this would happen", "the prepper", because as he says, he is always prepared - of course his conspiracy got proven correct by simple chance, lol.

The gameplay is surprisingly thought out. It plays in first person. You are able to loot almost any closet, briefcase, dumbster and infected. You can barricade doors with planks and move furnitare to block or open passages, place mines and of course throw molotovs or even flares for distraction. Melee combat is reasonably viable with the ability to push zombies away and punching those heads with occasional "finishing" prompts, the weaponry has the obligatory set of all different classes (pistol, shotgun, full auto, rifle, crossbow etc) that you gain by progressing and of course there are healing items that vary from chocolate bars to full fledged medical kits. Oh, lets not forget collectables in form of newsletters that add to the games lore and weapon upgrades that increase firerate and accuracy and such.

A nice little twist is the following: The game keeps running while in Menus. When opening the inventory, the camera gets out of first person, the character physically takes down his backpack and lets you know with certainty that you indeed are vulnarable while managing stuff. Same applies for looting.

In normal mode there is no respawn upon dying, your character permanently dies and you come in as another person that gets to reclaim your lost backpack and continue the story. Survival Mode removes that mechanic and you restart the entire game after dying which makes you act more careful by A LOT.

On a technical side, this port is bad. In order to have stable frametimes, you need to cap your frames to (optimally) 60 fps via gpu driver. There are non ignorable sound issues, the guns are almost completely silent just as explosions and certain doors. The gunplay works but feels very cluncy in terms of animations. Apparently there are a couple soft-lock situations when scanning CCTV boxes with zombies in proximity or when simply dying at wrong places because.. reasons? I myself got soft-locked when checking the CCTV monitors in the safe house that show you missed loot that you can pin to your map - this menu simply didn't let me close it. I googled possible "quick fixes" to not reload the safe because in this game (because survival horror huehue) you need to save manually by sleeping in the safe house - Had to do reload regardless because nothing helped and well, i lost 45 minutes of progress needing to redo the entire chapter.

I sincerely think this game is amazing for what ubisoft tried to accomplish, i can only imagine how good it would have played on the Wii U but this port however, it licks balls like a mf. I want to recommend it so bad but we also need to be honest about the technical problems that it has.

Thanks for reading.
